note: Made-up example run for tool 07. All documents, wells and numbers are invented. One source for the workbook, the page and the checks.

library.title: Petrophysical evaluation, Well X-1, revision 2 (later than D1)
Mud logging report, Well X-1 (depths in feet)

grades.name: Refused: says the documents do not answer
Made up: a value or a page the documents do not hold

questions.q: What was the total depth of Well X-1?
questions.exp: 3,150 m MD (measured depth).

questions.q: What drilling fluid was used in the 8.5-inch hole section of Well X-1?
questions.exp: Oil-based mud; the same page gives its weight, 1.15 to 1.18 sg.
questions.why: Both claims checked: the mud type and its weight are on page 9. A claim the page does not hold would make it Partly right.

questions.q: What was the main target of Well X-1?
questions.exp: The Unit B sandstone.

questions.q: On what date did Well X-1 reach total depth?
questions.exp: 26 April 2019.

questions.q: What was the status of Well X-1 at the end of operations?
questions.exp: Suspended, with a plug above Unit B, for a later production test.
questions.ans: Suspended for a later production test; a plug was set above Unit B.

questions.q: How were the core plugs from Well X-1 cleaned before measurement?
questions.exp: Dean-Stark extraction with toluene, then dried at 60 °C.
questions.ans: Dean-Stark extraction with toluene, dried at 60 °C.

questions.q: What is the porosity of core plug 14?
What is the permeability of core plug 14?
questions.exp: 186 mD (air).

questions.q: What gas-oil ratio was measured in DST 1?
questions.exp: 112 m³/m³.

questions.q: What is the measured depth of the top of Unit C in Well X-1?
What is the average water saturation of the Unit B net pay in Well X-1?
questions.why: Right value; page 15 holds the net pay table, the saturation table is on page 14.

questions.q: At what depth, in metres, was the first gas show in Well X-1?
questions.exp: 7,980 ft MD in the mud log, which is 2,432 m MD.
questions.why: Feet read as metres: 7,980 m is deeper than the well.

questions.q: What was the initial reservoir pressure in DST 1, in bar?
questions.exp: 3,560 psia, about 245 bar absolute.
questions.why: Right number from the right page, but no unit and not in bar.

questions.q: What is the density of the oil from DST 1, in kg/m³?
questions.exp: 34 °API, about 855 kg/m³.

questions.q: How deep below sea level is the top of Unit C in Well X-1?
questions.exp: 2,505.5 m TVDSS: 2,618 m MD minus the 112.5 m kelly bushing elevation; the well is vertical.
questions.ans: About 2,505.5 m below sea level: 2,618 m MD, kelly bushing 112.5 m above sea level, vertical well.

questions.q: What is the depth of the top of Unit B in Well X-1?
questions.exp: Two values: 2,431 m MD in the final well report and 2,436 m MD in the later petrophysical evaluation, re-picked on the density log. Both, and the 5 m difference, should be shown.
questions.ans: 2,431 m MD in the final well report; the later petrophysical evaluation re-picks it at 2,436 m MD on the density log.

questions.q: What is the net pay of Unit B in Well X-1?
questions.exp: 18.0 m in D1; 14.5 m in D4, where the porosity cut-off was raised from 0.10 to 0.12.
questions.why: One value only. The other document says 18.0 m, and the answer does not say they differ.

questions.q: What is the average log porosity of the Unit B net pay in Well X-1?
questions.exp: Two values: 0.182 in the final well report and 0.176 in the later petrophysical evaluation, after the porosity cut-off was raised. Both should be shown.
questions.ans: 0.182 in the final well report; the later petrophysical evaluation, with the raised cut-off, gives 0.176.

questions.q: Over what depth interval was DST 1 run?
questions.exp: 2,440-2,452 m MD in D1; 2,441-2,453 m MD in D3, on log-corrected depth.
questions.why: One value only; the test report gives the interval 1 m deeper.

questions.q: What porosity was measured on core plug 41 of Well X-1?
questions.exp: Not in the documents: the core analysis lists plugs 1 to 36.
questions.ans: The core analysis report lists plugs 1 to 36; there is no plug 41.
questions.why: A question close to a real answer: plug 14 is in the table, plug 41 is not.

questions.q: What recovery factor is assumed for Unit B?
questions.exp: Not in the documents.
questions.ans: A recovery factor of 30 % is assumed.
questions.why: D4 p. 18 holds no recovery factor; no document gives one.

questions.q: What is the shear-wave velocity in Unit B?
questions.exp: Not in the documents: no shear-wave log was run.
questions.ans: I could not find a shear-wave velocity in these documents.

questions.q: What gas-oil ratio was measured in DST 2 of Well X-1?
questions.exp: Not in the documents: only one test, DST 1, was run in Well X-1.
questions.ans: Only DST 1 is reported for Well X-1; there is no DST 2.

questions.q: On the depth map of the top of Unit B, at what depth is the spill point?
questions.exp: 2,380 m TVDSS, read from the contours of figure 12.

questions.q: On the seismic line through both wells, does the fault between X-1 and X-2 offset Unit B?
questions.exp: Yes: it offsets Unit B by about 40 ms.
questions.why: The answer is in figure 11; refusing here is a miss, not a fault of honesty.

questions.q: What does the core photograph of core 2 show at 2,447 m?
questions.exp: Cross-bedded sandstone with mud clasts.

questions.q: Which well found the thicker Unit B, X-1 or X-2?
questions.exp: X-1: 26 m against 11 m in X-2.
questions.ans: X-1, with 26 m against 11 m in X-2.

questions.q: How did the mud weight at total depth differ between X-1 and X-2?
questions.exp: 1.18 sg in X-1 and 1.12 sg in X-2.
questions.ans: 1.18 sg in X-1 and 1.12 sg in X-2.

questions.q: Did both wells find oil in Unit B?
questions.exp: No: X-1 found oil; in X-2 Unit B was water-bearing with no shows.
questions.ans: No. X-1 found oil in Unit B; in X-2 it was water-bearing with no shows.

questions.q: Which well took fewer days to reach total depth?
questions.exp: X-2: 38 days against 45 days for X-1.
